Title: Verify only shop owner can access order-related actions
Preconditions: User is logged in as a shop owner with at least one existing order in the system. A non-owner user account exists and is logged out.
Steps:
1. Log in as the shop owner.
2. Navigate to the Orders section.
3. Select an existing order to view its details.
4. Attempt to create a new order with valid input.
5. Attempt to update an existing order with valid input.
6. Log out.
7. Log in as the non-owner user.
8. Navigate to the Orders section.
9. Attempt to view any order details.
10. Attempt to create a new order with valid input.
11. Attempt to update any existing order with valid input.

Test Data: Shop owner credentials: {username: 'owner1', password: 'securepass'}. Non-owner credentials: {username: 'user1', password: 'userpass'}. Order details: {customerName: 'John Doe', customerPhone: '1234567890', items: [{itemId: 1, quantity: 1}]}
Expected Result:
1. Shop owner can successfully view, create, and update orders without any access errors.
2. Non-owner user receives an 'Access Denied' or 'Unauthorized' error message when attempting to view, create, or update any order.

Title: Verify Hibernate SQL formatting and debug logging are enabled and visible in application logs without breaking database operations
Section: Hibernate SQL Formatting and Debug Logging Configuration
Preconditions: 1. Application is deployed with the updated application.properties. 2. Database is accessible and contains test data (e.g., orders, items). 3. Logging level is set to DEBUG for the application.
Steps:
1. Trigger a database operation (e.g., retrieve an order or create an item). 2. Inspect the application logs for Hibernate SQL statements. 3. Verify the SQL statements are formatted (indented and readable). 4. Confirm DEBUG-level logs for org.hibernate.SQL are present.

Test Data: Old: No Hibernate SQL formatting or DEBUG logging. New: spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.format_sql=true, logging.level.org.hibernate.SQL=DEBUG
Expected Result: 1. Database operations complete successfully (e.g., HTTP 200 OK response). 2. Application logs show formatted SQL statements (indented, readable). 3. DEBUG-level logs for org.hibernate.SQL are present and include the executed SQL queries.
